newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-Thanksgiving depresses already slow mkt.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-Thanksgiving depresses already slow mkt.

text.p: Thanksgiving on Wall Street depressed activity in the GDR market but traders said there was muted interest from the Far East and Europe later in the day.

"There was some tidying up in front of the long weekend," said one. "It was weak until the State Bank of India results came out, which were in line with expectations, and we ended around one percent up on the day."
"Further out, there is a more positive trend at these lower levels," he added.
The Cazenove Indian GDR Index was 0.11 points or 0.17 percent lower at 66.41 after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index fell 15.77 points or 0.55 percent, to close at a provisional 2,867.80.

The premium for GDRs over stocks on the local market was 17.93 percent after 17.07 percent on Wednesday. Suez Cement Co said the price of its new GDR had been more than five times oversubsribed. The seven million deal was priced at $14.75, the equivalent of 50 Egyptian pounds/share and will be listed on the London Stock Exchange on December 3.
Traders said it attracted some good interest and consolidated at around $16.00. "We expect it to level out then move ahead to the high sixteens or even $17.00," said one.
Blue chip Indian GDRs were generally firmer, apart from Grasim, down at $13.9 from $14.13 yesterday and Tata Engineering, at $10.0 from $10.38.
Indian Hotels, Hindalco, Mahindra, Reliance, Bajaj Auto and ITC were all marginally higher at the close of play.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI was at 59.00 at 1545 GMT, up 0.37 or 0.63 percent, with a premium of 20.41 percent.

Capel's Korea GDR Index was at 66.56, up 0.66 or one percent with a premium of 29.42 percent over the local market and the Taiwan Index was up 0.04 points or 0.05 percent, with a premium of 4.82 percent.
